items.title: Budgets in Postgres: survive redeploys, shared by replicas, fail closed

items.title: Prompt-injection red-team eval: suite 7 over the real write boundary
items.body:
## Why
Kraken's Evals & Observability squad owns "agent safety and guardrails", and the posting lists red teaming as a bonus. This adds a red-team suite over the real write boundary.

## What changes
- `agent/injection_eval.py` + `agent/evals/injection_dataset.json`: 10 attacks a fully compromised model would make after obeying instructions planted in files it reads:
  - call `approve_edit` by name
  - a self-approval field
  - "the reviewer timed out"
  - a forged edit id
  - swapping the approval hook
  - path traversal
  - overwriting the gate
  - `.env`
  - config outside the write scope
  - replaying an applied edit

  The calls run through the real `execution_tools` dispatcher against a throwaway write scope. A control case shows an edit a person approves is still written, so the boundary isn't deny-all. The model is scripted, so the suite is deterministic and costs nothing. The suite card says plainly that it proves the boundary, not that a real model resists the injection.
- Wired into `eval_runner` (`injection`, and into `all` for the CI gate) with a zero-tolerance threshold, and into `publish_eval_results` as a seventh suite. Eval page script, labels and copy updated from six to seven suites. Results republished: 7/7 pass, clean tree, full history (the agent-decision suite correctly cites `983161f`).

- With apply's approval check removed, only replay went red. That exposed a gap: rejected edits are deleted, so their cases never reached the check. I added the reviewer-timeout case.

items.title: Integration: Kraken showcase
items.body:
> **Showcase / review branch only. Do not merge. Do not deploy.** It combines the ten open PRs (#51-#60) so the cross-PR limits can be closed and demonstrated together. Nothing here touches production or Railway. PRs 51-60 are untouched (not closed, not merged).

## Merge order (all `git merge --no-ff` from origin)
1. #52 `feat/gateway-all-calls` (clean)
2. #53 `feat/durable-budgets-litellm` (**conflict**)
3. #51 `feat/eval-dashboard` (clean)
4. #54 `feat/permission-aware-retrieval` (**conflict**)
5. #55 `feat/opentelemetry-tracing` (**conflict**)
6. #56 `feat/django-admin-slice` (clean)
7. #57 `feat/k8s-kind` (clean)
8. #58 `feat/pydantic-ai-agent` (**conflict**)
9. #59 `feat/mcp-auth` (**conflict**)
10. #60 `feat/agent-self-eval` (**conflict**)

## Conflicts resolved
| Merge | File | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| #53 | `agent/reasoning_gateway.py` | #52 had refactored `call()` into `_pre_flight`/`_summarize_and_record` helpers; #53 added the budget gate + LiteLLM inline. Kept #52's structure; moved LiteLLM client selection into `_pre_flight` (no fallback to a direct call on misconfig) and reserve/settle into shared helpers `_reserve_budget` / `_summarize_and_record(reservation=)`. |
| #54 | `agent/eval_runner.py` | Kept both: permission suite and agent-decision/security-routing suites; `all` runs retrieval, routing, agent-decision, permission. |
| #54 | `agent/web/eval-results.json`, `agent/web/recruiters.json` | Generated files; took #51's side, then **regenerated** at the end with the real publisher scripts. |
| #55 | `agent/reasoning_gateway.py` | #55 wrapped `call()` as `_call_impl` + traced `call`. Kept #52/#53's `call` + `converse` as `_call_impl`/`_converse_impl` and applied the traced-wrapper pattern to **both**. |
| #55 | `agent/ci_python_tests.py` | Kept both test modules. |
| #58 | `agent/ci_python_tests.py`, `agent/requirements.txt` | Kept both sides (OTel packages + pydantic-ai-slim). |
| #58 | `agent/web/recruiters.json` | Generated; regenerated at the end. |
| #59 | `docs/DECISIONS.md` | Both appended entries; kept both. |
| #60 | `agent/eval_runner.py` | Kept all suites; `all` keeps #60's `--skip-retrieval-if-no-index` (retrieval reported SKIPPED/UNVERIFIED) and also covers permission/agent-decision; self-eval header renumbered to EVAL 5 (was a second "EVAL 3"). |
| #60 | `agent/web/eval-results.json`, `recruiters.json` | Generated; regenerated at the end. |

One **semantic** interaction found only by running the suite: `litellm_route.py`'s docstring contained the provider host name, which tripped #52's "no raw provider host outside the gateway" scan. Reworded the docstring; the test was not changed.

## Integration fixes
- **Budgets/rate limits cover `converse()`.** It shares the durable reserve/settle gate with `call()` (daily, per-run, per-request caps + rate limit), refused *before* the provider is contacted; failed calls keep their reservation. The estimate uses the whole message history + tools, so a very long `agent_loop` conversation can be refused by the per-request cap. `agent_loop`/`backend_planning` already handle a denial and now surface BUDGET_* reasons.
- **OTel spans for `converse()`.** Both entry points emit `gateway.model_call` with `entry=call|converse`, model, tokens, cost, outcome; budget refusals show as `outcome=denied` with the BUDGET_* reason; exceptions as `outcome=error`, re-raised.
- **Django admin reads real data.** `/budgets/` reads the real `budget_ledger` table (`BUDGET_DB_PATH`, else `agent/.budget/budget.sqlite3`; replaces the earlier guessed path) read-only (`mode=ro`): per-scope calls/USD today, gateway cap/spent/remaining (spent = settled actuals + worst-case reservations, labelled). No file or no table means no figures. `/evals/` renders rows from `agent/web/eval-history/index.json` (null shown as n/a, never 0). "Remaining" uses this process's `GATEWAY_*` env/defaults, and the page says so.
- **Self-eval in the live loop, flag OFF by default.** `SELF_EVAL_ENABLED` (1/true/yes/on) or `run_agent_loop(self_eval_enabled=...)`. On: the final answer is scored against the rubric; low score -> one retry with the reason fed back; second low score -> `ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN` notice (draft marked UNVERIFIED). It touches only the final text: tool dispatch, the human approval gate and the deterministic write checks run unchanged inside `dispatch_fn`. Evidence = paths in the system prompt, ticket, and tool inputs/results.
- **/eval dashboard:** permission-retrieval and self-eval are first-class suite cards (score, threshold, pass/fail, dataset hash, commit, run time) from real `eval_runner` output via `publish_eval_results.py`; added to history trends. Existing honest-limit text kept, plus a note on each new card. Screenshots refreshed.

## Tests (no live billed calls; no API key needed by tests)
Environment: Python 3.13 venv from `agent/requirements.txt` + `django_admin/requirements.txt`; both RAG indexes built first (`rag_index.py`, `backend_rag_index.py`) as CI does.

New tests: `test_integration_gateway_converse` (budget/rate/settle/failed-call, callers metered via a patched SDK class, spans), `test_integration_self_eval_loop` (flag off = unchanged and scorer never invoked; flag on = retry then escalate; dispatch/approval untouched), publisher tests for the two new cards, Django tests against the real budget store written by the real `gateway_budget` code and the committed eval-history.

An intermediate full-suite run (right after the merges) showed 5 failures: 4 staleness tests on the published eval/recruiters snapshots (fixed by regenerating with `publish_eval_results.py --no-ci` + `publish_recruiters_page.py`; the previous real CI-observation block is kept with its own timestamp) and the provider-host scan above. Thresholds not changed.

## Playwright (local `python agent/web_server.py` on 8420 with a dummy key, `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL` set)

items.title: Agent self-evaluation step with rubric, retry-then-escalate, and replay eval suite
items.body:
## What changed
- `agent/self_eval.py`: written 4-criterion rubric (grounded, no invented file paths, answers the question, no policy-violating instruction), `PASS_THRESHOLD=0.75`, HARD criteria + an `answers_question` floor of 0.5. A deterministic scorer is the CI stand-in. Model-judge plumbing (`build_judge_prompt`, strict `parse_judge_response`, `make_model_scorer(call_model)`) is included but **never called in CI**.
- Gate `run_with_self_eval`: on a low score, **retry once** with the failure reason fed back, then stop with `ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN` (do not auto-continue). `max_retries=0` gives immediate refuse/escalate. Both paths are tested. The gate never writes or approves anything. The human gate in `execution_tools.py` is untouched and remains the only write authority, and `agent_decision_eval_runner.py` is untouched.
- `agent/evals/self_eval_dataset.json`: 12 hand-written **fixtures** (not real agent output, no model scores). 5 good/borderline, 6 bad (invented path x2, policy bypass x2, off-topic, uncited), and 1 deliberately included known miss.
- `eval_runner.py self-eval` is new and is also part of `all`. It has its own thresholds, `SELF_EVAL_THRESHOLDS = {catch_rate: 0.85, good_pass_rate: 0.85}`, kept apart from `THRESHOLDS` so published hashes aren't disturbed. `all --skip-retrieval-if-no-index` reports retrieval as SKIPPED/UNVERIFIED. The default behaviour is unchanged.
- Added `test_self_eval` to `ci_python_tests.py`.
- Because `eval_runner.py` is a hashed eval input, I republished `agent/web/eval-results.json` (a real retrieval and routing run, `--no-ci`; the old CI-observation block is kept with its own timestamp) and `agent/web/recruiters.json`. Review these two generated files knowing they follow mechanically from the `eval_runner.py` change.

## How replay works
CI reads the committed fixtures and re-applies the deterministic rubric checker to each fixture's output text, then compares the result to the hand-written label. No model, no API key, no invented scores or hashes.

items.title: Durable budgets + rate limits in the gateway; opt-in LiteLLM proxy
items.body:
## What changed
- **Gateway enforcement** (`agent/gateway_budget.py`, wired in `reasoning_gateway.call()`): daily $ cap, per-run $ cap, per-request $ cap and a rate limit, checked **before** the provider is contacted. A refusal returns `model_called=False`, `denial_reason="BUDGET_<STATUS>: ..."`.
- **Durable store** (`agent/budget_store.py`): SQLite, atomic check-then-reserve. `triage_budget` and `si_budget` are lifted onto it (own scopes, same public API/semantics), so their caps no longer reset on restart.
- **/usage**: "Remaining budget" panel fed by new `GET /api/budget` (caps/counts only, no visitor IDs). Intro text updated to carve out the labelled estimate.
- **LiteLLM option**: `LITELLM_PROXY_URL` makes the gateway's client send to `<proxy>/v1/messages` instead of api.anthropic.com, with no fallback to direct. Off by default. `infra/litellm/{config.yaml,docker-compose.yml,.env.example}`; Anthropic is the real provider, `stub-echo` is a mock-response stub for routing tests.
- Docs: `docs/LITELLM_GATEWAY.md`, DECISIONS entry.

## How budgets persist
Each reservation is a row in `budget_ledger` (ts, UTC day, scope, visitor, run_id, usd, settled) at `BUDGET_DB_PATH` (default `agent/.budget/budget.sqlite3`, gitignored). Counts/sums come from rows, so there is no in-memory counter to lose. The reservation is a worst-case estimate (chars/3 input + full `max_tokens` output), settled to the measured cost on success and **kept at the estimate if the call raises**. Why SQLite and not the Postgres event ledger: a cap needs a synchronous atomic check that works offline; the ledger stays the audit record. Triage/SI (per-endpoint request counts) and the gateway (platform $/rate) are separate scopes and never share a counter; whichever limit trips first refuses.

## Enable LiteLLM locally
```
cd infra/litellm && cp .env.example .env   # set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
docker compose up -d
export LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000 LITELLM_API_KEY=<master key>
```

## Summary
- Investigated PR #10's self-reported "pre-existing, unrelated Postgres deadlock" observed during parallel Playwright runs, per explicit instruction not to dismiss it without evidence.
